(i) a corpus of annotated ad hoc structures is a useful resource for developing algorithms for their extraction and analysis, (ii) the combination of spatial and token category features is a promising basis for identifying ad hoc structures in text, and (iii) a simple combination of distributional and alignment techniques is a promising basis of record and field identification in ad hoc structures.

(1) a diverse sample of naturally occurring structured regions can be collected and annotated, (2) probabilistic segmentation methods, featurized with spatial and token category skip bigrams, can be used to identify contiguous regions of text that share a single structure type, and (3) a combination of distributionally similar and sequence aligned records can be identified with minimal supervision in the case of key-value lists, and with a combination of distribution, alignment, and token category similarity in the case of tables.

(i) the use of spatial and token category skip bigrams as features for text segmentation improves performance over a baseline, and (ii) the combination of distributional similarities and sequence alignment improves performance over either approach in isolation.
